summary: Preserved PR 2543's subprocess isolation, eight-second timeout, and singleflight overload response while correcting the three HTTP-contract regressions independently reported by PR 3259. The request query and Accept/Accept-Encoding headers are now passed to the isolated child, which uses Prometheus' own exposition negotiation before returning status, headers, and body to the ASGI endpoint.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before comparison against prometheus_client.make_asgi_app: the candidate included unrelated beta_total for name[] filtering, omitted gzip Content-Encoding, and returned Prometheus text 0.0.4 for an OpenMetrics Accept header.
Passing-after real ASGI/multiprocess comparison: name[] excluded beta_total, gzip was negotiated, and OpenMetrics returned application/openmetrics-text, matching the reference exporter.
Five focused tests passed for HTTP negotiation/filtering, event-loop isolation and singleflight, timeout cleanup, child failure, and cancellation cleanup.
The candidate's retained isolation fixture returned 200 for the active scrape, 503 for the overlapping scrape, and measured 0.001 seconds event-loop lag.
Changed Python files compiled and the patch had no whitespace errors.

gpu_execution.evidence: No GPU was used because the corrected behavior is confined to CPU-side ASGI request negotiation and Prometheus multiprocess-file exposition. Exercising the available gfx950 would not validate this defect.

remaining_limitations: The original eight-H100 multi-node single-tokenizer PD deployment, real sustained scrape pressure, bootstrap read timeouts, and decode-side connection-loss logs were unavailable and were not claimed as reproduced.
The deterministic isolation fixture validates event-loop protection and overload behavior, not a full distributed/model workload.

Prometheus' existing MultiProcessCollector name[] behavior may return an empty restricted response because the collector registers without metric-name descriptors; this correction deliberately preserves the prior make_asgi_app contract and, critically, no longer returns unrelated metrics.
